newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen at DM400 in "grey" trade - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen at DM400 in "grey" trade - dealers.

text.p: Shares in German steel group Thyssen AG were trading for as much as 400 marks in unofficial trade on Tuesday after being suspended from official trade, dealers said.

The shares, which closed IBIS electronic trade at 344.50 marks on Monday, are being pushed to extreme highs because of speculation that industrial group Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp is poised to make a takeover bid for Thyssen.
Both Krupp and Thyssen were suspended from trading on Tuesday morning.
Thyssen, describing the situation as serious, said that Krupp was poised to make a hostile takeover bid and said it was prepared to defend itself against the threat.
"There are rumours coursing through the market that small shareholders are to be offered 430 to 450 marks," said a Frankfurt dealer.

Dealers said several thousand Thyssen shares had changed hands at 400 marks, but that demand had fallen off somewhat in the early afternoon. The shares had shot up to 395 marks at the start of unofficial trade, dealers said.
However unofficial trading in Krupp shares had been unspectacular, dealers added.
